sections.label: Corporate Income Tax rebate changes
sections.summary: The CIT rebate for YA 2018 is raised to 40% capped at $15,000, and extended to YA 2019 at 20% capped at $10,000.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, the existing Corporate Income Tax (CIT) rebate for the Year of Assessment (YA) 2018 will be enhanced by raising the rebate percentage from 20% to 40% of tax payable, and the rebate cap from $10,000 to $15,000.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The CIT rebate will also be extended to YA 2019, at 20% of tax payable, capped at $10,000.

sections.label: R&D tax deduction increase
sections.summary: Tax deduction for staff costs and consumables on qualifying R&D projects performed in Singapore is increased from 150% to 250%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Third, to encourage research and development (R&D) to be done in Singapore, the tax deduction for staff costs and consumables incurred on qualifying R&D projects performed in Singapore will be increased from 150% to 250%.

sections.label: Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation cap
sections.summary: The expenditure cap for Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation claims without prior approval is raised from $100,000 to $150,000 per YA from YA 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Fourth, to further encourage internationalisation, the expenditure cap for the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation claims, without prior approval from Enterprise Singapore or the Singapore Tourism Board, will be raised from $100,000 to $150,000 per YA from YA 2019.

sections.label: IRAS sharing information with law enforcement
sections.summary: The Income Tax Act is proposed to be amended to allow IRAS to share information with law enforcement agencies for investigation or prosecution of serious crimes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The second broad change pertains to the proposed amendment of the Income Tax Act to allow IRAS to share with law enforcement agencies (LEAs) information that may be necessary for investigation or prosecution of serious crimes.

sections.label: Tax deduction for PHC drivers
sections.summary: PHC drivers may claim tax deduction on car-related expenses against driving income, based on a deemed expense ratio of 60% of gross driving income.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In view that taxi and PHC drivers now provide similar point-to-point transport services, we will allow tax deduction on car-related expenses incurred by PHC drivers, against their driving income.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And to keep compliance manageable, a PHC driver may claim tax deduction for expenses incurred to earn driving income based on a deemed expense ratio prescribed in the Income Tax Act.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We consulted with the National Private Hire Vehicles Association and the National Taxi Association and have proposed to set the deemed expense ratio at "60% of gross driving income".

sections.label: Effective date of amendments
sections.summary: The proposed amendments will take effect from YA 2019, for income earned in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments will take effect from YA 2019, for income earned in 2018.

sections.label: PHC drivers' income tax expenses
sections.summary: PHC drivers asked why expenses like petrol and parking cannot be deducted against income, leaving them with higher income tax.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Early this year, when it was about time to file for income tax return, many PHC drivers whom I met – some I met at coffee shops, some they came to my Meet-the-People Session, and they asked why is it that the expenses, such as petrol, car parking are not allowed to be deducted against their income, and end up they have to pay higher income tax.

sections.label: Extending tax claim to delivery persons
sections.summary: It asks whether the Minister will consider including other self-employed delivery persons if PHC drivers can claim income tax.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If PHC drivers can claim income tax, will the Minister consider the inclusion of other self-employed delivery persons as well?

sections.label: Minimum mileage for tax deduction
sections.summary: It suggests PHC drivers must meet a minimum mileage or number of jobs requirement to enjoy the tax deduction.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This would be unfair to the full-time drivers.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I, therefore, suggest that for a PHC driver to enjoy the tax deduction, he must also meet a minimum mileage or number of jobs requirement.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill and hopes it takes effect before next year's income tax filing.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (In English): Sir, I support the Bill and I hope that it will come into effect before the filing of income tax for next year.

sections.label: Contribute-As-You-Earn MediSave model
sections.summary: The Government accepted the Tripartite Workgroup's Contribute-As-You-Earn model requiring MediSave contributions when a service fee is earned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government has accepted the Tripartite Workgroup's recommendations for "Contribute-As-You-Earn" model whereby a MediSave contribution is required as and when a service fee is earned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And intermediaries and corporate service buyers are required to make the deductions whenever they pay the self-employed person.

sections.label: Insurance and tax incentives
sections.summary: The Government accepted a recommendation on insurance products for self-employed persons, and it asks about tax incentives for gig workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government has also accepted the Tripartite Workgroup's recommendation that the tripartite partners work with insurers to make available to self-employed persons insurance products that will provide daily cash payouts in the event of loss of income due to prolonged illness or injury.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider tax incentives to encourage the take-up of such insurance products by gig economy workers, including along the lines of existing income tax relief for life insurance?

sections.label: Grab PHC driver revenues
sections.summary: Grab informs that its full-time PHC drivers have gross revenues between $6,400 and $10,800 per month.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Grab informs me that their full-time PHC drivers have gross revenues between $6,400 and $10,800 per month.

sections.label: PHC and taxi driver tax
sections.summary: The Bill reduces a full-time PHC driver's tax by about $1,800 to $4,700 a year and affects 97,000 taxi driver licence holders.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under the proposed Bill, a full-time PHC driver will have a reduction in tax in the range from about $1,800 to $4,700 a year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Their tax burden will be substantially reduced by this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill will also affect our 97,000 taxi driver licence holders, who can now choose to have their deductions computed by formula.

sections.label: Self-employed own account workers
sections.summary: MOM reports that in 2017, 8.4% of Singaporean workers were self-employed own account workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) reports that in 2017, 8.4% of Singaporean workers were self-employed own account workers.

sections.label: Donation and BIPS extensions
sections.summary: The passage lists the extension of the tax deduction for qualifying donations and the extension of BIPS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the extension of the tax deduction for qualifying donations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, the extension of the Business and Institutions of a Public Character (IPC) Partnership Scheme (BIPS).

sections.label: Permanent deduction after 2021
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister would consider formalising the deduction as a permanent measure after 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Would the Minister consider formalising the deduction as a permanent measure after 2021?

sections.label: Section 14ZB BIPS extension
sections.summary: Section 14ZB will extend the Business and IPC Partnerships Scheme for another three years until December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, section 14ZB will similarly extend the Business and IPC Partnerships Scheme for another three years until December 2021.

sections.label: Driver expenses and MediSave payments
sections.summary: A driver's $33,000 expenses are not deductible and rising MediSave payments make basic necessities hard to meet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: His total expenses for this year come up to $33,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: None of this can be categorised as deductibles and, on top of that, he has to make MediSave payments that keep on increasing and, therefore, he has problems meeting expenses for his basic necessities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: If car rental payments, along with other expenses incurred on the job were made tax-deductible, the situation would be fairer.

sections.label: Tax deductions for PHC drivers
sections.summary: Allowing PHC drivers to claim tax deductions for expenses will help them manage their costs of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Allowing PHC drivers to claim tax deductions for expenses will help them to manage their costs of living.

sections.label: Tax deduction for qualifying donations
sections.summary: The 250% tax deduction for qualifying donations was extended three years until December 2021 to encourage giving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: First, on tax deductions for qualifying donations and extension of the Business and IPC Partnership Scheme (BIPS) which were raised by Mr Louis Ng, the 250% tax deduction for qualifying donations was extended for three years until December 2021 to continue to encourage the spirit of giving.

sections.label: Business and IPC Partnership Scheme
sections.summary: BIPS, piloted in the second half of 2016 to encourage business volunteering, was extended three years in 2018 until December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Unlike tax deduction for qualifying donations, BIPS is a relatively new scheme that was first piloted in the second half of 2016 to encourage businesses to support their staff to volunteer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We extended the scheme for three years in 2018 until December 2021 as the take-up was encouraging.

sections.label: Deemed expense ratio for drivers
sections.summary: A tax deduction based on a deemed expense ratio of 60% of gross driving income applies to full-time and part-time drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Indeed, this is a reason why IRAS has taken time to listen to feedback from different stakeholders and, instead of coming up with a scheme that may be complicated and different to administer, we have decided on a tax deduction based on the deemed expense ratio set at 60% of gross driving income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This ratio is a proxy for all expenses incurred to earn driving income and it applies to both full-time and part-time drivers.

sections.label: Contribute-As-You-Earn MediSave model
sections.summary: A Contribute-As-You-Earn model for self-employed persons' MediSave contributions will be piloted by 2020, with the Government leading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Government is very mindful of this issue and that is why we have mandated to start with MediSave account contributions by self-employed persons to ensure that they are able to meet their basic healthcare needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And as several Members have highlighted, MOM announced in this year's Committee of Supply that the Government would be implementing a "Contribute-As-You-Earn" model for self-employed persons' MediSave contributions whereby a MediSave contribution is required as and when a service fee is earned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Government, as a service buyer, will take the lead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we will implement the "Contribute-As-You-Earn" model, starting with a pilot by 2020.

sections.label: IRAS officers enhanced investigative powers
sections.summary: Enhanced investigative powers in the amendment Bill will be exercised only by authorised IRAS officers, who will undergo training on use of force and other techniques.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I had mentioned earlier in my speech just now, the enhanced investigative powers in the amendment Bill will be exercised only by authorised IRAS officers and they will undergo training on the use and escalation of force and various other techniques that are relevant to the exercise of these enhanced investigative powers.

sections.label: Arrest without warrant tax offences
sections.summary: Arrest without a warrant may be exercised only for investigating serious tax offences like tax evasion or where a suspect destroys evidence to hinder IRAS investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For example, the power to arrest without a warrant may only be exercised for an investigation of serious tax offences like tax evasion or where a suspect attempts to destroy evidence with a view to hindering or obstructing IRAS' investigations.
